GB uses decimal units; GiB uses powers of 1024. A 16 GB chip is about 14.9 GiB before partitions. The rough remainder subtracts reported data use and listed filesystem capacities from the candidate disk size. Other partitions, reserved blocks, shared mounts, a different disk or altered reports can make it wrong. It is not a measurement of writable free space; an independent, non-destructive device check is needed.

Android 14 normally reports API 34 or newer and contains the tested Android 14 class. A mismatch suggests an altered or customized system, but the release, SDK and kernel can also be modified. These checks cannot authenticate the exact Android base version.
Android reports %1$s GiB RAM, while the kernel reports %2$s GiB. The cause and physical chip size are not verified.
Possible storage mismatch: /data reports %1$s GB, while candidate %2$s reports %3$s GB. Check that this disk backs /data; firmware can also affect these readings.
Android %1$s is reported, but the reported SDK is API %2$d. Android %3$d normally requires API %4$d or newer.
Android %1$s and API %2$d are reported, but the Android 14 framework class probe is unavailable. The framework may be inconsistent or customized.
Android 14 API marker present (also present in newer versions)
Off: launcher only. On: show the individual switches. Turning Expert on again restores saved choices, so a previously enabled file hub may start automatically.
Press OK on each switch. Turning a feature off stops its associated work where possible. Memory savings vary by device; no fixed saving is guaranteed.
On, but paused until Expert mode is on.
Show the in-app header and clock on the Home and Tools screens. It does not affect the floating status pill, which has its own switch.
Allow on-demand captures. Turning this off does not delete saved screenshots; an enabled file hub can still share them.
Start the local listener while the TV Guard activity exists. It can expose Downloads and saved screenshots; the warning above applies. It can start again when Expert is restored.
Allow browser keys, text, app launches and installation prompts. Requires the file hub. Remote screenshot and boost also require their own switches.
Run hardware and root evidence checks when enabled or refreshed. A root manager may prompt; reported readings cannot authenticate the device.
Scan packages and check for root only while its screen is open. A root manager may prompt. Review choices before removing anything.
Probe internet and common router addresses when the diagnostics screen opens or is retested.
Allow an on-demand attempt to stop background apps and, if root is available, drop kernel caches. Results vary.
Scan processes while the Tools overview is open. Android may restrict which processes are visible.

Warning: the file hub has no password or encryption. Anyone on the local network may view, upload or delete Downloads and saved screenshots; enabled remote controls can operate the TV. Use only a trusted network and turn it off when finished.
Check available ports and storage access, or turn the file hub off in Expert settings.
File sharing is off. Turn on the file hub in Expert settings if needed.
Showing CPU load, available RAM, storage and network quality over other apps.

Draws the five readings on one line at the top of the screen: processor load, free RAM, free storage, temperature and internet quality. Needs "Display over other apps". Secure or system screens may hide it.
Allow "display over other apps" to use the overlay.
Android hides overlays over secure or system screens such as DRM video and some dialogs. There is no supported workaround, so the pill may not appear there.

Read-only check of ADB debugging, apps allowed to install from unknown sources, device admins, accessibility services and the default HOME app. Each line links to its system screen. Nothing is changed until you open one.
Nothing is changed here. Each line links to the system screen where that setting lives; a link opens that screen, and only there can anything be changed.
No issues found in the settings visible to this app; this is not a security guarantee.
Alerts: %1$d; warnings: %2$d. Open the linked screens to review.
Security shield in the status strip
Adds a sixth cell to the floating pill: secure, review or alert, from the checks below. Needs the status pill on.
The status pill is off, so the shield is not drawn yet.
Debugging can allow an authorized computer to control the device. Network debugging exposes it over the network; pairing or authorization is normally required. The network status may be unavailable.
Apps allowed to install from unknown sources
These apps may request APK installs from outside a store; Android may still require confirmation. One or two is a review; three or more is an alert.
A managed device can be controlled remotely by the company or provider that set it up. An admin app only has the policies it was granted.
An accessibility service can read the screen and inject input. One may be deliberate; several is an alert. Keep only the ones you installed on purpose.
Compared with the HOME app recorded at the previous launch. Opening this screen acknowledges a change.
Some security settings could not be read. No clear result is available.
That screen is not available on this TV.

Shizuku is not running or TV Guard is not authorized. Open Shizuku, start it using its supported setup, then allow TV Guard. Starting it may require user pairing or root and may be needed again after reboot.

Process visibility depends on Android and the TV. RSS includes shared memory and must not be added as exact app RAM. Recently used is not the same as running. Storage numbers are filesystem reports, not proof of physical capacity.
